The other string is inclined at an angle of $30^\circ$ to the horizontal, as shown in Figure 1. The tension in the horizontal string is $Q$ newtons and the tension in the other string is $P$ newtons. Find

parts.label: a

(3)

questions.stem: A particle $P$ of mass 2 kg is moving under the action of a constant force $\mathbf{F}$ newtons. When $t=0$, $P$ has velocity $(3\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and at time $t=4$ s, $P$ has velocity $(15\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the acceleration of $P$ in terms of $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$,
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: $\mathbf{a} = \dfrac{(15\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j})-(3\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})}{4} = 3\mathbf{i}-1.5\mathbf{j}$ M1 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) the magnitude of $\mathbf{F}$,
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
N2L $\mathbf{F} = m\mathbf{a} = 6\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j}$ ft their $\mathbf{a}$ M1 A1
$|\mathbf{F}| = \sqrt{6^2+3^2} \approx 6.71$ (N) M1 A1 accept $\sqrt{45}$, awrt 6.7

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) the velocity of $P$ at time $t=6$ s.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\mathbf{v}_6 = (3\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})+(3\mathbf{i}-1.5\mathbf{j})6$ ft their $\mathbf{a}$ M1 A1ft
$= 21\mathbf{i}-7\mathbf{j}\ (\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})$ A1

questions.question_text:
A particle $P$ of mass 2 kg is moving under the action of a constant force $\mathbf{F}$ newtons. When $t=0$, $P$ has velocity $(3\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and at time $t=4$ s, $P$ has velocity $(15\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Find
(a) the acceleration of $P$ in terms of $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$,
(2)
(b) the magnitude of $\mathbf{F}$,
(4)
(c) the velocity of $P$ at time $t=6$ s.
(3)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
$\mathbf{a} = \dfrac{(15\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j})-(3\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})}{4} = 3\mathbf{i}-1.5\mathbf{j}$ M1 A1
N2L $\mathbf{F} = m\mathbf{a} = 6\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j}$ ft their $\mathbf{a}$ M1 A1
$|\mathbf{F}| = \sqrt{6^2+3^2} \approx 6.71$ (N) M1 A1 accept $\sqrt{45}$, awrt 6.7
$\mathbf{v}_6 = (3\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})+(3\mathbf{i}-1.5\mathbf{j})6$ ft their $\mathbf{a}$ M1 A1ft
$= 21\mathbf{i}-7\mathbf{j}\ (\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})$ A1

questions.stem: A ball is projected vertically upwards with speed 21 $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ from a point $A$, which is 1.5 m above the ground. After projection, the ball moves freely under gravity until it reaches the ground. Modelling the ball as a particle, find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the greatest height above $A$ reached by the ball,
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
$v^2 = u^2+2as \Rightarrow 0^2 = 21^2-2\times9.8\times h$ M1 A1
$h = 22.5$ (m) A1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) the speed of the ball as it reaches the ground,
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
$v^2 = u^2+2as \Rightarrow v^2 = 0^2+2\times9.8\times24$ or equivalent ($=470.4$) M1 A1
$v \approx 22\ (\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})$ A1 accept 21.7

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) the time between the instant when the ball is projected from $A$ and the instant when the ball reaches the ground.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
$v = u+at \Rightarrow -\sqrt{470.4} = 21-9.8t$ or equivalent M1 A2 (1,0) $-1$ each error
$t \approx 4.4$ (s) A1 accept 4.36

questions.question_text:
A ball is projected vertically upwards with speed 21 $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ from a point $A$, which is 1.5 m above the ground. After projection, the ball moves freely under gravity until it reaches the ground. Modelling the ball as a particle, find
(a) the greatest height above $A$ reached by the ball,
(3)
(b) the speed of the ball as it reaches the ground,
(3)
(c) the time between the instant when the ball is projected from $A$ and the instant when the ball reaches the ground.
(4)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
$v^2 = u^2+2as \Rightarrow 0^2 = 21^2-2\times9.8\times h$ M1 A1
$h = 22.5$ (m) A1
$v^2 = u^2+2as \Rightarrow v^2 = 0^2+2\times9.8\times24$ or equivalent ($=470.4$) M1 A1
$v \approx 22\ (\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})$ A1 accept 21.7
$v = u+at \Rightarrow -\sqrt{470.4} = 21-9.8t$ or equivalent M1 A2 (1,0) $-1$ each error
$t \approx 4.4$ (s) A1 accept 4.36

questions.stem:
Figure 3

A box of mass 30 kg is being pulled along rough horizontal ground at a constant speed using a rope. The rope makes an angle of $20^\circ$ with the ground, as shown in Figure 3. The coefficient of friction between the box and the ground is 0.4. The box is modelled as a particle and the rope as a light, inextensible string. The tension in the rope is $P$ newtons.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the value of $P$.
(8)
parts.mark_scheme:
Use of $F = \mu R$ B1
$P\cos20^\circ = \mu R$ M1 A1
$R+P\sin20^\circ = 30g$ M1 A1
$P\cos20^\circ = \mu(30g-P\sin20^\circ)$ M1
$P = \dfrac{0.4\times30g}{\cos20^\circ+0.4\sin20^\circ}$ M1
$\approx 110$ (N) A1 accept 109

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The tension in the rope is now increased to 150 N.
(b) Find the acceleration of the box.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
$R+150\sin20^\circ = 30g$ M1 A1 ($R\approx242.7$)
N2L $150\cos20^\circ-\mu R = 30a$ M1 A1
$a \approx \dfrac{150\cos20^\circ-0.4\times242.7}{30}$ M1
$= 1.5\ (\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}})$ A1 accept 1.46

questions.stem:
Figure 4

Figure 4 shows two particles $P$ and $Q$, of mass 3 kg and 2 kg respectively, connected by a light inextensible string. Initially $P$ is held at rest on a fixed smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The string passes over a small smooth light pulley $A$ fixed at the top of the plane. The part of the string from $P$ to $A$ is parallel to a line of greatest slope of the plane. The particle $Q$ hangs freely below $A$. The system is released from rest with the string taut.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Write down an equation of motion for $P$ and an equation of motion for $Q$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
N2L $Q$: $2g-T = 2a$ M1 A1
N2L $P$: $T-3g\sin30^\circ = 3a$ M1 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Hence show that the acceleration of $Q$ is 0.98 $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
$2g-3g\sin30^\circ = 5a$ M1
$a = 0.98\ (\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}})$ * A1 cso

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the tension in the string.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
$T = 2(g-a)$ or equivalent M1
$\approx 18$ (N) A1 accept 17.6

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) State where in your calculations you have used the information that the string is inextensible.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: The (magnitudes of the) accelerations of $P$ and $Q$ are equal B1

parts.label: e
parts.text:
On release, $Q$ is at a height of 0.8 m above the ground. When $Q$ reaches the ground, it is brought to rest immediately by the impact with the ground and does not rebound. The initial distance of $P$ from $A$ is such that in the subsequent motion $P$ does not reach $A$. Find
(e) the speed of $Q$ as it reaches the ground,
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
$v^2 = u^2+2as \Rightarrow v^2 = 2\times0.98\times0.8\ (=1.568)$ M1
$v \approx 1.3\ (\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})$ A1 accept 1.25

parts.label: f
parts.text:
(f) Find the time between the instant when $Q$ reaches the ground and the instant when the string becomes taut again.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
N2L for $P$: $-3g\sin30^\circ = 3a$ M1 A1
$a = (-)\dfrac{1}{2}g$
$s = ut+\dfrac{1}{2}at^2 \Rightarrow 0 = \sqrt{1.568}\,t-\dfrac{1}{2}4.9t^2$ or equivalent M1 A1
$t = 0.51$ (s) A1 accept 0.511

A maximum of one mark can be lost for giving too great accuracy.
